title: Effect of incretin-based and nonpharmacologic weight loss on body composition: a systematic review
authors: Batsis JA, Gavras A, Gross DC, Cheever CR, Da Silva BR, Meira Filho LF, et al.
population: 35 randomised trials of liraglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide or dulaglutide in adults reporting fat mass, fat-free mass, lean soft tissue, muscle indices or visceral fat by BIA, DXA, CT or MRI; median duration 26 weeks, median 78 participants; search January 2003 to February 2026
funder: Primary funding source: none, as stated in the structured abstract. Disclosure forms are available online and were not read.
result: Within incretin groups the median share of total weight loss from muscle-based indices was 28.3% (IQR 15.9% to 39.9%), with 65% of interventions exceeding a prespecified benchmark of about 25%; by BIA or DXA about 29% (16.6% to 43.1%), 67% above benchmark; by CT or MRI about 25.3% (16.7% to 27.2%), two thirds above a 15% benchmark. Among 13 lifestyle or placebo comparator groups, with median weight change of -2.5%, 38% exceeded the benchmark. No study reported objective physical function. 42.9% of studies were at low risk of bias and 28.6% prespecified body composition as a primary outcome; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis.
